- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 3–7% if recent history shows sustained upward momentum.
- When true outcome shows strong upward trend after a spike, model tends to overcorrect; apply a “mean reversion” buffer to avoid premature peak prediction.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome in the first 5–10 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day to align with observed downward drift.
- For long-term forecasts (e.g., 30-day), avoid over-optimistic tail-end predictions; cap forecast at 1.5–2x the 30-day moving average of recent history.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; add a “lag correction” rule: if true value drops below 10% of peak in 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 10–20%.
- Avoid forecasting above 35% above the 30-day moving average unless accompanied by strong macroeconomic or policy signals (e.g., EU ETS auction changes).
